title: Redwood Optimize Walkthrough - Batching & KV Cache - Alpha Payments
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and KV/prefix caching recommendations for Alpha Payments' conversational assistant. Discussed workload characteristics, expected hit rates, cost model scenarios, and pilot next steps. Agreed to run benchmarks and share a cost spreadsheet and security docs.
action_items: Priya Nair (Redwood SE): run 24h pilot benchmark using Alpha Payments' sample workload, capture latency and token counts - due 2026-12-08
Carlos Mendes (Alpha CTO): share representative prompt set and session distribution (histogram of session lengths) - due 2026-12-04
Jordan Lee (AE): send optimized cost model spreadsheet and Redwood security overview (SOC2 + SSO details) - due 2026-12-02
next_steps: Redwood to run pilot on hosted/test cluster and return results in 1 week
Alpha to confirm pilot traffic window and whitelist IPs for test cluster
Schedule follow-up to review pilot results and discuss Dedicated sizing if needed
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Samir (Product), Carlos (Alpha CTO), Aisha (Lead ML), Ben (Infra), Maya (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: okay everyone thanks for joining, quick check, audio ok?
[00:05] Carlos: yep sounds good, thanks Jordan, excited to dig in.
[00:12] Jordan: awesome. we'll do a quick agenda - walkthrough of Redwood Optimize recommendations focused on batching and the prefix / KV cache model, then cost modeling, then Q&A and next steps. Priya you wanna kick off?
[00:28] Priya: sure, I'll share my screen - give me a sec. so first question for you Aisha and Ben - what's your current traffic shape? mean session length, percent of multi-turn sessions, that kind of thing.
[00:42] Aisha: we see about 180k sessions per day, average session length is 6 turns but heavy tail up to 40, about 25% multi-turn >10 turns, and many short info lookups.
[00:58] Ben: infra-wise we're on GCP, kubernetes, and we're open to dedicated instances but need to justify cost.
[01:08] Priya: perfect. those numbers actually map well to some of the common savings we see with KV cache. quick primer: prefix cache stores repeated starting prefixes across sessions so you avoid re-tokenizing and re-running attention for common opening prompts; KV cache (per-session) lets you resume without recomputing previous tokens. in practice you get best results when you combine both: prefix cache for repeated prompts and KV for longer in-session continuity.
[01:35] Carlos: couple clarifying q's — how do you handle privacy? we can't send PII to hosted models in raw form.
[01:44] Jordan: good question — we have encryption at rest, optional customer-managed KMS in Private or Dedicated, and token redaction policies you can apply before sending. we'll attach full security docs but briefly SOC2 + SSO/SAML supported.
[02:00] Priya: back to batching - we recommend continuous batching with latency SLO knobs. tradeoff is higher batching gives better throughput (lower cost per token) but increases tail latency. for Alpha Payments your 95th latency target?
[02:18] Carlos: under 350ms for user-facing flows, background jobs can be higher.
[02:25] Priya: okay so we'll show two scenarios: conservative batching (target p95 < 300ms) and aggressive batching (p95 ~ 400-500ms) for background workloads.
[02:36] Samir: and remind us about quantization / model variants impact? we run a custom fine-tuned model on Llama-3 variant.
[02:44] Priya: right - quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) reduce GPU memory & cost but we need to validate quality. Redwood supports model routing so you can route low-risk traffic to quantized variant and high-risk to fp16. we included both in the cost model.
[02:58] Priya: now I'll pull up the cost model spreadsheet - baseline is current hosted run with no cache and per-token inference.
[03:07] Priya: baseline numbers (approx): unoptimized cost: $0.16 per 1k tokens served (example), average tokens per session 1,200 -> monthly ~ $35k. with prefix+KV caching we estimate token delta reduction 30-45% depending on hit rate.
[03:30] Aisha: that percent range depends heavily on how many repeated prompts we have?
[03:34] Priya: exactly. prefix cache helps when you have repeated system or onboarding prompts - in payments flows we often see the same verification prompts and help texts. if you have high repetition of system prompts and templates you'll see higher prefix hit.
[03:46] Ben: what's realistic hit-rate for us with our dataset?
[03:49] Priya: based on similar customers with mixed multi-turns, we model 20% (low), 35% (typical), 50% (high) prefix hit. KV cache improves long sessions - for sessions >8 turns you'll see 60-85% effective token savings on subsequent turns. combined effect yields ~35% total token reduction in the typical model we showed.
[04:10] Jordan: I'll note: these are modeled estimates; pilot benchmarking is recommended to get your exact numbers.
[04:17] Carlos: ok can you show me the pilot plan?
[04:20] Priya: yes - pilot outline: we spin up a test cluster with 4 GPU workers on Redwood hosted sandbox (or we can run in your Dedicated trial), replay a representative 24h window of traffic, measure tokens, throughput, latencies, and cache hit rates. expected time 48-72h to produce a report.
[04:37] Maya: will the test use our actual prompts? we have templates with PII placeholders.
[04:42] Priya: yes, you can provide prompt templates with placeholders; we support local masking / redaction prior to sending. you can also run with synthetic masked data.
[04:50] Aisha: what about cold-start impact on KV cache? we have many ephemeral sessions.
[04:55] Priya: cold-start is real - initially KV cold means no savings for first turn; but prefix cache can give immediate savings for repeated starting prompts even across ephemeral sessions. also we pre-warm frequent prefixes. in the cost model we included a 10% warmup period for new features.
[05:12] Jordan: show of numbers — with typical 35% reduction we modeled monthly savings from $35k to $23k (~$12k savings). aggressive tuning + dedicated capacity can push to 50% reduction in some workloads.
[05:25] Ben: that'd justify dedicated if committed throughput is high, yes. what's the recommended Dedicated sizing?
[05:30] Priya: for your peak we estimate 6 A100-equivalent workers for p95 < 350ms with conservative batching; can be lower with higher batch latency tolerance. we'll include a Dedicated sizing sheet in the cost model.
[05:42] Samir: one subtlety — how does KV cache work across shard / pod boundaries? will we lose cache benefit if a session routes to different worker?
[05:51] Priya: good callout. Redwood's KV cache is session sticky by default (session affinity) for Dedicated; in hosted we route with sticky tokens, and we also offer shared distributed prefix cache to get cross-worker reuse for common prefixes. we'll describe the fallback policy: if affinity not possible we route to the next best model with a warmup recommendation.
[06:10] Carlos: latency numbers — what p50/p95 should we expect with prefix cache hits?
[06:15] Priya: p50 typically drops 10-25% with good prefix hits because we avoid reprocessing early layers; p95 improvement depends on batching dynamics but can often be similar or slightly worse if aggressive batching is used; that's why we tune the SLO.
[06:30] Jordan: quick aside on instrumentation - Redwood Console surfaces token-level cost, per-route latency, and per-model KV/prefix cache hit rate. you'll be able to see a dashboard for this pilot.
[06:40] Aisha: nice. can we set alerts for regression on quality when using quantized models?
[06:45] Priya: yes - Optimize ties quality monitoring to eval prompt sets; you can create canaries and threshold alerts. we'll include a sample eval set in the pilot to measure syntactic and semantic regression.
[06:58] Carlos: ok show the spreadsheet cells for the model assumptions.
[07:02] Priya: (screen) baseline token per session 1,200; sessions/day 180k; monthly tokens ~ 6.48B. compute cost baseline $X per token (we anonymized in the deck but we'll send exact numbers in spreadsheet). with prefix hit 35% we reduce billed tokens by 2.27B monthly.
[07:26] Aisha: micro question - do you bill on request tokens or model tokens after cache?
[07:31] Priya: Redwood bills on served model tokens post-caching. so if prefix prevents model from re-evaluating tokens you aren't billed for those.
[07:40] Ben: what about partial hits? if only part of the prefix matches, how is it counted?
[07:44] Priya: partial prefix matches reduce the number of tokens sent to the model proportionally; we approximate billing on exact tokens executed. imperfect speech sometimes in transcribe: 7:44 partial prefix partial hits -> reduce tokens.
[07:55] Jordan: next section - concrete recommendations for Alpha Payments: 1) enable prefix cache for common onboarding / auth prompts, 2) enable KV cache for multi-turn flows above 3 turns, 3) set conservative batching for user-facing flows, aggressive batching for offline jobs, 4) pilot to validate hit rates.
[08:15] Carlos: safe defaults sound good. I worry about memory blowup with KV for long sessions - we've seen on our infra memory spike.
[08:24] Priya: we recommend per-session KV TTL and a cap on KV size (max tokens cached per session) - common pattern is cap at 4k tokens; older tokens can be dropped or summarized. we can also offload cold KV segments to cheaper storage and stream them back if needed (warm-up penalty).
[08:44] Aisha: summarization automated? that sounds useful.
[08:47] Priya: yes Redwood has optional summarization hooks to compress older context into a short summary that you can keep in the session state instead of full KV. quality tradeoff must be measured in evals.
[08:58] Jordan: question from Samir - can we do hybrid routing: hosted for low-latency public stuff, Dedicated for high-volume private flows?
[09:06] Priya: absolutely. Redwood supports policy-based routing by route, user class, or region. you can have the same model catalog with different variants pinned per route.
[09:16] Samir: what about regional compliance? EU-resident data needs to stay in region.
[09:20] Jordan: we can pin to EU region or offer Private deployment; we'll attach details for VPC/Private options and KMS integration.
[09:28] Carlos: let's dig into the metric outputs from your pilot - what will you provide?
[09:32] Priya: we'll provide: token counts pre/post caching, prefix hit rate by prompt template, KV hit rate by session length bucket, latency p50/p95/p99, cost breakdown per route, CPU/GPU utilization, and a suggested Dedicated sizing.
[09:48] Aisha: great. a couple more technicals - cache consistency: if we update system prompt, how do you invalidate prefix caches?
[09:55] Priya: we version prefixes and provide TTL/invalidate APIs; you can purge on rollout. we recommend rolling updates with canaries.
[10:05] Ben: operator view - are these caches stored in Redis/managed store?
[10:09] Priya: for hosted we use a managed in-memory distributed cache optimized for prefixes, backing store is a sharded K/V layer; in Dedicated you can choose managed or bring-your-own Redis for prefix metadata; KV cache for session residues lives in worker memory with optional spill to a persistent store.
[10:26] Samir: does the prefix cache use fuzzy matching or exact match? sometimes we change wording but same intent.
[10:31] Priya: prefix cache supports template-based matching and hashed canonicalization; we also support fuzzy similarity thresholds for templated prompts. in the pilot we can tune threshold to maximize hit without hurting precision.
[10:44] Jordan: quick demo snippet - here's the Console showing per-route token usage with cache overlay (visual). (screen) you can see the blue line pre-cache and green post-cache.
[10:56] Carlos: cool. can Redwood handle bursts? holiday spikes expected for us.
[11:01] Priya: autoscaling + burst capacity works. Dedicated has reserved pools plus burst pools; Hosted elastically scales but you pay for the peak. cost model shows commit vs burst tradeoffs.
[11:12] Carlos: show the commit math one more time - how do you amortize reserved cost?
[11:16] Priya: reserved gives lower unit cost per token; we recommended committed capacity only if you have predictable baseline traffic. we included a break-even chart in the spreadsheet - for Alpha Payments at current numbers break-even ~ 6 months at 40% utilization.
[11:33] Aisha: ok more on instrumentation - can we map cache hit rate back to user ids to see which users benefit?
[11:39] Priya: yes per-route/per-session tagging available; you can filter by user cohorts in Console. PII controls apply and you'd want to pseudonymize ids.
[11:49] Ben: how do you treat retries? if a request fails and retries go to new worker, do we double-bill missed cache?
[11:56] Priya: retries only billed on actually executed tokens; if the retry re-evaluates from scratch you'll be billed accordingly. we also have idempotent routing helpers to reduce double work.
[12:08] Carlos: any gotchas on summarization & regulatory audit trails? if we summarize PII out of record that might be an issue.
[12:15] Priya: we recommend redaction-first then summarization; Redwood stores both raw (encrypted) and summarized artifacts depending on retention policy and compliance needs. retention and audit logs are configurable.
[12:28] Jordan: jumping ahead to pilot timeline - assuming you share sample prompts by Friday (Dec 4) we can start pilot next week and have a report by Dec 10-12.
[12:39] Carlos: yes we'll share.
[12:42] Maya: one more pricing nuance: does the cost model include tokenization overhead or only model compute?
[12:48] Priya: it includes both. tokenization is minor but included in CPU cost; most savings come from skipping model compute with caching.
[12:57] Aisha: what about GPU memory fragmentation with large KV caches?
[13:01] Priya: that's why we cap per-session KV, use spilling, and sometimes summarize old context. it prevents OOM.
[13:10] Samir: can we see an example of a cache hit event in logs?
[13:14] Priya: yes (screen) here's an event: request id -> matched prefix id -> hit true -> served tokens 56 (instead of 420). console shows the delta.
[13:26] Ben: network overhead - prefix cache lookups add an RTT, does that hurt small requests?
[13:31] Priya: prefix lookup is optimized and co-located; overhead is <2ms on average. for extremely latency-sensitive single-turn requests we sometimes disable remote lookup and rely on local heuristics.
[13:45] Carlos: ok let's talk risk - what are the main failure modes?
[13:49] Priya: 1) cache staleness (invalidated by prompt change) - mitigated by versioning and TTL, 2) memory pressure - mitigated by caps & spill, 3) quality regression from quantized models - mitigated with eval canaries, 4) unexpected routing leading to missed affinity - mitigated by sticky session routing.
[14:08] Jordan: question - have you tried KG/persistent context approaches?
[14:11] Aisha: we use a small vector DB for entity lookups in some flows.
[14:15] Priya: Redwood can integrate with vector DBs for retrieval augmentation; that's complementary to prefix/KV caches. retrieval reduces model tokens too but is another tradeoff.
[14:25] Carlos: I'd like to see the pilot results speak - are you able to simulate a holiday spike during pilot?
[14:30] Priya: yes we can run synthetic bursts; recommended to do a run with normal traffic + 2x burst window to measure autoscaling.
[14:40] Ben: ok on security side please share SOC2 & KMS integration docs.
[14:44] Jordan: will do. we'll attach those in the follow-up.
[14:48] Priya: wrapping into a quick micro-case - we ran a similar workload for another fintech and saw 38% token savings and 22% latency improvement p50 using prefix+KV plus conservative batching. that customer moved to Dedicated after 3 months.
[15:05] Carlos: interesting. can you share anonymized benchmark?
[15:08] Priya: yes we'll include anonymized run in the attachments.
[15:12] Maya: what about support SLAs during pilot?
[15:15] Jordan: pilot includes SE support; if moving to Dedicated we can include a premium SLA.
[15:20] Carlos: good. couple final questions on integration - do you have SDKs for session affinity?
[15:26] Priya: yes we have SDKs and examples for session tokens, sticky headers, and sample code for kv TTL management.
[15:34] Aisha: about data residency again - if we run Hosted EU only, will prefix cache share data across EU tenants?
[15:41] Priya: no, tenant isolation is enforced; prefix metadata is namespaced per-tenant unless you explicitly configure shared cache for cross-tenant templates (rare).
[15:52] Ben: misc: what's the overhead of running summarization? cost wise?
[15:56] Priya: summarization is additional model compute but you can schedule it offline; cost depends on frequency and length - we included a sample amortized cost in the spreadsheet.
[16:08] Samir: about rollout: how do we A/B test prefix caching?
[16:12] Priya: we recommend canary route with 10% traffic using prefix+KV, compare quality metrics (ROUGE/semantic) and latency/cost. Redwood Console automates the split and collects delta metrics.
[16:24] Carlos: ok seems comprehensive. two more items: 1) can you estimate the cost delta if we use quantized vs fp16 for our model? 2) what's the expected ops churn to maintain caching rules?
[16:33] Priya: 1) quantized often saves 20-40% on GPU cost; we included scenario lines for 8-bit and 4-bit in the model. 2) ops churn is low after initial tuning - mostly updating prefix templates when prompts change, and occasional TTL adjustments. we'll include a runbook.
[16:50] Jordan: looping back to next steps: we'll run pilot, share cost model, attach security docs, and meet next week to review.
[16:58] Carlos: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[17:02] Jordan: thanks all - we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and pilot checklist.
[17:10] (call ends)

Note: transcript contains minor transcription artifacts and speaker label approximations.
questions: How are cache hits billed? (model tokens after caching)
What's realistic prefix hit rate for our workload?
How to invalidate prefix caches on prompt changes?
Can we run pilot with masked PII data?
